description: The image presents two pie charts comparing the distribution of different error types in Chinese spelling correction, as analyzed in the paper “A Coin Has Two Sides: A Novel Detector-Corrector Framework for Chinese Spelling Correction.” The left chart, titled “All Changes,” illustrates the proportions of six categories: PW (light green, 50%), R (light yellow, 26%), RW (golden yellow, 14%), NW (blue, 5%), N (light blue, 1%), and an unlabeled gray slice (4%). The right chart, “All Errors,” shows a similar breakdown: PW (56%), R (29%), RW (6%), NW (5%), N (1%), and the gray slice (3%). Both charts use color-coded slices with percentage labels and share a common legend on the right, indicating that PW, R, RW, N, and NW correspond to specific error or correction types, while the gray slice’s label is not provided in the legend. The charts visually emphasize the dominance of PW in both total changes and total errors, with R and RW also contributing significantly, while N and NW remain minor components.
